newsitem.title: FINLAND: UPM SAYS MAY SELL AAMULEHTI SHARES.
newsitem.headline: UPM SAYS MAY SELL AAMULEHTI SHARES.

text.p: Finnish forest industry group UPM-Kymmene Oy said on Wednesday it had a preliminary agreement to sell 362,324 Aamulehti series I shares to Swedish media group Tidnings AB Marieberg .

"The sale of the shares is contingent on approval of the merger from the annual general meetings of Aamulehti and MTV," UPM-Kymmene said in a statement, referring to the merger plan announced on Tuesday between the media group and the domestic broadcaster.
Marieberg said on Tuesday it had agreed to buy that number of shares, raising its stake in Aamulehti to 28.8 percent of shares and 28.45 percent of votes after full conversion of debt into equity.
Marieberg said on Tuesday it would keep its target to own 20 percent of the group formed by the Aamulehti/MTV Oy merger and slated to be launched at early in 1998.
Already the single biggest Aamulehti shareholder, Marieberg would also be the single biggest owner in the new merged group, Aamulehti said on Tuesday.
